cases.prompt: The entire front of head and neck has a partial-thickness burn. What percentage of adult TBSA is burned?
cases.tip: The whole head and neck is 9%; one surface is 4.5%.

cases.prompt: The entire back of head and neck has a partial-thickness burn. What percentage of adult TBSA is burned?
cases.tip: The whole head and neck is 9%; one surface is 4.5%.

cases.prompt: The entire front of right arm has a partial-thickness burn. What percentage of adult TBSA is burned?
cases.tip: One surface of an arm is half of the whole arm: 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5%.

cases.prompt: The entire front of left arm has a partial-thickness burn. What percentage of adult TBSA is burned?
cases.tip: One surface of an arm is half of the whole arm: 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5%.

cases.prompt: The entire back of right arm has a partial-thickness burn. What percentage of adult TBSA is burned?
cases.tip: One surface of an arm is half of the whole arm: 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5%.

cases.prompt: The entire back of left arm has a partial-thickness burn. What percentage of adult TBSA is burned?
cases.tip: One surface of an arm is half of the whole arm: 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5%.

cases.prompt: The entire chest has a partial-thickness burn. What percentage of adult TBSA is burned?
cases.tip: The chest and abdomen are separate 9% regions. Upper and lower back are also separate 9% regions.

cases.prompt: The entire abdomen has a partial-thickness burn. What percentage of adult TBSA is burned?
cases.tip: The chest and abdomen are separate 9% regions. Upper and lower back are also separate 9% regions.

cases.prompt: The entire upper back has a partial-thickness burn. What percentage of adult TBSA is burned?
cases.tip: The chest and abdomen are separate 9% regions. Upper and lower back are also separate 9% regions.

cases.prompt: The entire lower back, including buttocks has a partial-thickness burn. What percentage of adult TBSA is burned?
cases.tip: The chest and abdomen are separate 9% regions. Upper and lower back are also separate 9% regions.

cases.prompt: The entire front of right leg has a partial-thickness burn. What percentage of adult TBSA is burned?
cases.tip: One surface of a leg is half of the whole leg: 18 ÷ 2 = 9%.

cases.prompt: The entire front of left leg has a partial-thickness burn. What percentage of adult TBSA is burned?
cases.tip: One surface of a leg is half of the whole leg: 18 ÷ 2 = 9%.

cases.prompt: The entire back of right leg has a partial-thickness burn. What percentage of adult TBSA is burned?
cases.tip: One surface of a leg is half of the whole leg: 18 ÷ 2 = 9%.

cases.prompt: The entire back of left leg has a partial-thickness burn. What percentage of adult TBSA is burned?
cases.tip: One surface of a leg is half of the whole leg: 18 ÷ 2 = 9%.

cases.prompt: The entire perineum has a partial-thickness burn. What percentage of adult TBSA is burned?
cases.tip: The perineum is 1% total. It is not counted separately on the front and back.

cases.prompt: The entire right arm, front and back, has partial-thickness burns. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: A whole arm includes both surfaces: 4.5 + 4.5 = 9%.

cases.prompt: The entire left leg, front and back, has partial-thickness burns. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: A whole leg includes both surfaces: 9 + 9 = 18%.

cases.prompt: The entire head and neck, front and back, has partial-thickness burns. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Do not confuse one side of the head and neck with the whole region.

cases.prompt: The entire anterior trunk (chest and abdomen) has partial-thickness burns. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Chest 9% + abdomen 9% = anterior trunk 18%.

cases.prompt: The entire posterior trunk, including buttocks, has partial-thickness burns. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: The buttocks are included in the posterior trunk. Do not add them again.

cases.prompt: Partial-thickness burns cover the entire right arm (front and back) and the entire anterior trunk. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Separate whole limbs from single surfaces before adding.

cases.prompt: Both entire legs, front and back, have partial-thickness burns. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Each whole leg is 18%. Both entire legs are 36%.

cases.prompt: Only the entire front of each leg has partial-thickness burns. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Two front surfaces are 9 + 9, not 18 + 18.

cases.prompt: Partial-thickness burns cover the entire front of the head and neck and the entire front of the right arm. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Two 4.5% surfaces combine to 9%.

cases.prompt: Partial-thickness burns cover the entire posterior trunk and the entire front of the left arm. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Use 18% for the posterior trunk and 4.5% for one arm surface.

cases.prompt: Partial-thickness burns cover the entire right leg and the entire head and neck, including front and back of both regions. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Whole leg 18% + whole head and neck 9%.

cases.prompt: Partial-thickness burns cover the entire back of both arms. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Each posterior arm surface is 4.5%.

cases.prompt: Partial-thickness burns cover the entire chest and the entire back of the left leg. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Chest alone is 9%; it does not include the abdomen.

cases.prompt: Partial-thickness burns cover the perineum and the entire left leg, front and back. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Add the perineum’s 1% once.

cases.prompt: Partial-thickness burns cover the entire anterior trunk and the entire front of both legs. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Anterior trunk is 18%; each anterior leg is 9%.

cases.prompt: Partial-thickness burns cover the entire back of the head and neck and the entire back of the right leg. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Keep the head’s 4.5% separate from the leg’s 9%.

cases.prompt: Partial-thickness burns cover both entire arms (front and back) and the entire chest. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Both whole arms total 18%. Add only the chest’s 9%.

cases.prompt: A partial-thickness burn covers exactly half of the chest. The abdomen is unaffected. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Half of the chest means half of 9%, not half of the entire 18% anterior trunk.

cases.prompt: A partial-thickness burn covers exactly half of the front of the right leg. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: First choose the surface (front leg = 9%), then multiply by one half.

cases.prompt: Partial-thickness burns cover exactly half of each surface of the right arm: half of the front and half of the back. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Each half-surface contributes 4.5 × 0.5 = 2.25%. Add both halves.

cases.prompt: Partial-thickness burns cover half of the front of the right leg and the entire left arm, front and back. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Half of 9% is 4.5%. A whole arm is 9%.

cases.prompt: The entire anterior trunk has partial-thickness burns. The entire right arm has only superficial epidermal redness, with no partial-thickness injury. Calculate the TBSA included in burn-size estimation.
cases.tip: Superficial epidermal burns are excluded. Partial-thickness burns are included.

cases.prompt: The entire front of the left arm has superficial partial-thickness burns, and the entire back of the right leg has full-thickness burns. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: “Superficial partial-thickness” still counts. Do not confuse it with superficial epidermal injury.

cases.prompt: Partial-thickness burns cover the entire head and neck, front and back, plus the perineum. Calculate adult TBSA.
cases.tip: The perineum is a single 1% region, not 1% on each side.

cases.prompt: Partial-thickness burns cover half of the abdomen. Full-thickness burns cover the entire back of the left leg. The entire chest has only superficial epidermal redness. Calculate included adult TBSA.
cases.tip: Multiply the abdomen’s 9% by one half, include the 9% leg surface, and exclude superficial epidermal redness.
